draft.title: The Church in everyday life
card: In medieval Europe, the Christian Church was part of daily life for almost everyone. Villagers went to church on Sundays and holy days, and the priest marked births, marriages and deaths.
a tax of about a tenth of a person's produce or income, paid to the Church. Peasants often paid it in grain, animals or other goods.
communities of monks who lived by religious rules. Before printing existed, monks copied books by hand, which helped keep learning alive.
Monasteries also cared for the sick. Monks gave travellers and poor people food, shelter and basic medical care.
draft.remember: The Church took a tithe from people, and monasteries kept books and cared for the sick.

a.q: What was the tithe in medieval Europe?
opts: A payment of about a tenth of produce to the Church
A payment of about a tenth of produce to the king
A payment of about a tenth of produce to the lord
A fee of about a tenth of wages paid to a monastery for care
a.why: The tithe was a tax of about a tenth of a person's produce, paid to the Church. The tempting option is the lord, since peasants also owed the lord, but the tithe went to the Church.
a.clue: Think about who received the tenth.

b.q: Brother Tomas lives in a monastery in France in 1100. There is no printing press. How could he help keep learning alive?
opts: By printing books on a press
By collecting the tithe from villagers
By teaching soldiers how to fight
b.why: Without printing, books had to be copied by hand, and monks did this work in monasteries. Collecting the tithe was a different job: it raised money for the Church but did not keep books or knowledge safe.
b.clue: Books were made one at a time.

a.best: A payment of about a tenth of produce to the Church
